item.title: Contratto di ricerca: NATPRED: Naturalistic Predictions: How our brain anticipates the future in a dynamic world (Univ. TRENTO)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-16 12:00
Institution: Univ. TRENTO, Trento
Field: History, philosophy, education, psychology / 11/PSIC-01 Psicologia generale, neuropsicologia e neuroscienze cognitive, psicometria

We recently developed a new approach in the lab that combines MEG recordings of participants observing naturalistic dynamic input (e.g., movies), with dynamic representational similarity analysis (dRSA) to quantify both the strength and the millisecond-precision latency of neural representations of naturalistic dynamic input, across hierarchical levels of stimulus complexity (from perceptual-to-conceptual). See [4,5] for relevant previous research from the lab. This fully-funded postdoc position is part of a larger 5-year project funded by the Italian government (FIS starting grant) on which several PhD/postdocs will work. item.title: Contratto di ricerca: Comparative evaluation procedure for n. 1 research contract - Department of History and Cultures (Univ. BOLOGNA)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-10-27 12:00
Institution: Univ. BOLOGNA, Bologna
Field: History, philosophy, education, psychology / 11/HIST-01 Storia medievale

Title of the project: “Landed Wealth, Loans to Agriculturists and Exchange Rates in Genoa between the Twelfth and the Thirteenth Centuries” - The Genoese archives house the earliest collection of notarial registers of Latin Europe, which constitute an invaluable source for the economic history of the medieval Mediterranean. However, the prevailing interest in Genoese international trade has overshadowed the study of rural economy and of small-scale moneylending from citizens to rural dwellers – two research avenues that deserve further investigation. It should also be emphasised that the Genoese commune was perhaps the first to be granted the right to mint its own coin (in 1138). Moreover,…

item.title: Contratto di ricerca: Leggere la Sicilia attraverso il Viaggio in Italia di Goethe: tra storia della cultura, letteratura, arti e paesaggi (Univ. CATANIA)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-10-22 12:00
Institution: Univ. CATANIA, Catania
Field: History, philosophy, education, psychology / 11/PHIL-05 Storia della filosofia

This research, which spans the history of philosophy and literature as well as the Digital Humanities, aims to produce a digital edition of the section of Goethe’s Viaggio in italia devoted to Sicily, where the German writer travelled between March and May 1787. The edition, in which the text is presented in an Italian translation updated in line with the latest critical and philological findings on the work, will take the form of a ‘Hyperedition’, that is, a system of integrated resources comprising texts, images, commentaries and geomapping. item.title: Contratto di ricerca: PROMOTING THE SUSTAINABILITY OF FOOD SYSTEMS. Rethinking the Territorial Dimensions of Food in Light of the Challenges of Justice, Sustainability, Cultural Identity, and Local Development (Univ. CATANIA)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-10-22 12:00
Institution: Univ. CATANIA, Catania
Field: History, philosophy, education, psychology / 11/GEOG-01 Geografia

The project aims to develop models for food policy through a critical re-examination of the relationships between food and space (i.e., territory), with particular attention to urban, local, and global scales. It considers sustainability as a property of food systems that integrates social, economic, environmental, and governance dimensions. The objective is to contribute to the development of new food policies capable of addressing, in an integrated manner, the main challenges facing contemporary society and, consequently, contemporary food systems. These include food security and access to food; food justice and democracy; health understood in terms of well-being and safety; environmental…

item.title: Contratto di ricerca: Research contract in Coptic Studies as part of the MASLAB project: (ROMA "La Sapienza")
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-10-25 23:59
Institution: ROMA "La Sapienza", Roma
Field: History, philosophy, education, psychology / 11/HIST-04 Scienze del libro, del documento e storico-religiose

MASLAB investigates the transformations in the exercise of episcopal power within Christian communities in the Near East (7th–10th centuries) during the transition from Byzantine and Sasanian rule to Islamic rule. Drawing on a diverse, multilingual corpus of sources, the project analyzes how episcopal authority, relational networks, and the resources available to bishops adapted, reorganized, and redefined themselves within the new political and religious structures of the Islamic Empire. The project combines qualitative and quantitative methods to map bishops and dioceses of the Islamic period while comparing the experiences of various Eastern Christian traditions.
